title: Leaving Sol - Battle for Castor
author: pottrell
selftext:
Testing my game this morning and found myself in a full scale battle between two factions. I've realised, I need some battle music! Do you guys try to make your own? Source royalty free? 

\---

I've loved space games for years, particularly EVE and Elite, but these days I rarely get the time to sit down at a PC and properly play them.

I've always fancied something with that same sense of scale and progression, but something I could pick up on my phone, set a course, get on with my day and come back to later.

I couldn't find quite what I was looking for, so I started making it myself!

It's called Leaving Sol - https://www.leavingsol.com - A free multiplayer space game!

The idea is, you're an exploration ship's AI that has somehow become sentient. Every other player is another version of the same AI, all sharing one persistent galaxy.

You explore, mine using drone swarms, manufacture, trade, haul cargo across systems, develop skills (very much inspired by my RuneScape days), complete quests (both main story and sub stories), hunt down hostile mobs, and delve into long-lost asteroid 'dungeons'. Along the way you'll occasionally get into trouble with pirates and a long dormant hostile race.

Flight is Newtonian, planets follow real orbits, and journeys can take minutes or longer. The Bobiverse books were definitely a big inspiration for the underlying idea.

Why share it now?

The game is starting to come together. I've got a single-player build running on my phone, and combat went in this week, which has opened up hunting down mobs and exploring the asteroid dungeons.

The next big milestone is building the multiplayer server. Before I disappear down that rabbit hole, I thought I'd start sharing it to see if anyone else is interested other than me.

A little about how it's built

I'm enjoying the technical side almost as much as making the game itself, so a few details for anyone interested:

Built in Unity 6, but all the actual game logic lives in a separate C# library. This means the future multiplayer server and the phone will run exactly the same rules. There's around 540 automated tests and a simulation that runs weeks of in-game economic activity to check things don't fall apart.

The galaxy contains around \\\\\\\*\\\\\\\*100 million star systems\\\\\\\*\\\\\\\*, generated deterministically so every player sees exactly the same universe. Sol's real stellar neighbours are positioned accurately. I would note, as the game progresses, more of the generated systems will be tweaked/built on.

Newtonian flight, Keplerian planetary orbits, fixed-step physics and double precision.

 Ships and stations are modelled in Blender using Python scripts. Even the sound effects are generated programmatically using Python.

It started life as a browser prototype before I moved everything into Unity.

I've made extensive use of Claude Code along the way. I'm a developer during the day, so AI has been a huge help getting something of this scope off the ground. The ideas, design decisions and direction are mine, albeit inspired by what I've also seen, with AI assisting heavily with implementation. Because of the development approach, it's meant I've been able to play with Blender/Unity with some nice base models to learn the software instead of starting from scratch.

Anyway, that's enough of an introduction. I'd genuinely appreciate any thoughts, particularly from people who have played similar games or have experience with mobile game development.

Thanks for reading!

comments.author: Emma_Anderson96
comments.body: the idea of an EVE style space game designed around shorter mobile sessions is really interesting, how are u planning to make exploration feel rewarding across such a massive galaxy?

replies.author: pottrell
replies.body:
Still working on areas here but initially, being able to set up your own relay/station that connects to the rest of the network to establish trade routes, etc. This gives massive amounts of xp alongside your player name being attached to the system "chartered by...". There's various quests and contracts that ask you to go further out too. That's not including the trade/hauling business aspect too. A station may want you to deliver goods from station X to Y. 

Lots of planning and testing still to do

replies.author: revel911
replies.body:
It’s actually not as people slate saying 

<- 25 year UI / UX designer.

I would get very exact with interaction placement, then work on unique but recognizable iconography, then afterwards, find an icon branding that matches the game.

As to the game, I don’t love its MP, but gameplay looks hella fun.

replies.author: pottrell
replies.body:
100% agreed. I'm going to push to prioritise this earlier so we can establish a core component library, icon set, and UI design system right out of the gate. I think this is where I'd need to get some real testers in.

​I take a similar rule based approach to visual worldbuilding. 

Take the faction in this clip: it's an ocean world, so every piece of technology from ship architecture to weaponry like grapplers and harpoons strictly follows naval design rules.

comments.author: darkoblivion000
comments.body:
The idea is cool and at first glance it’s pretty exciting.

Needs work though. The ui buttons are all over the place and ttaking up a lot of real estate. Ships are clipping through each other left and right. First 6s there’s like a ship floating sideways appearing to get dragged by another ship? Is that a tractor beam intentionally? Looked weird

The capital ship looks like less detailed than the other ships. There are asteroids floating around but idk if they are supposed to be under the ship layer or not bc the ship goes right over it. The ship physics seem floaty in general, there’s no acceleration or deceleration mechanics you just seem to turn any which way 

There are specs of light or balls of light just floating around. I don’t know what they’re supposed to be - they kind of just make the scene look busy but if you were actually in space I don’t think you’d see random nondescript floating glowing balls

The flashes of light are a little much. I feel like you might give someone an epileptic seizure. The depth is kind of random feeling. Sometimes a missile flies in and it hits 2 ships. Sometimes another missile flies in visually the exact same way and goes right through. Doesn’t seem consistent at all how that works

replies.author: pottrell
replies.body:
I'll look into your feedback properly later, thanks for all the details! 

A few initial notes:   
The dragged ship was harpooned - a dynamic still in development. 
Ships intentionally can overlap to stop malicious players blocking.  
Completely agree with the UI  
Capital ships haven't been detailed yet - definitely on my list!  
This fight is taking place in an asteroid belt, so that's probably why it's coming across busy - notes though!

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
Ah I figured it was a tractor beam or something. Harpoon in space is interesting lol

I like the overall feel. In case you wanted to compare, another similar space game I played the demo of that I enjoyed was sublight. So maybe worth checking out and comparing notes
